rows.evidence: Q1: Section III Results and Figures 4-5 report the authors' own prototype (Arduino set-up with soil moisture sensor node, LED indicator) and the data sensed by the soil moisture sensor during operation.
rows.notes: The study is a design-and-prototype paper: it describes an IoT soil-moisture-based automatic pump control with farmer alerts and shows only that the sensor senses moisture and the LED/pump turns on and off according to stored thresholds. It reports no crop yield, productivity or water-use measurement of its own; the statements that the system improves water use and increases yield (Conclusion) are assertions, not results. Hence no own evidence on the claimed effect (enhanced agricultural productivity); the prototype functioning is at most a precondition of the claimed effect. Technology (IoT sensor-based scheduling with web/mobile notification) matches app_scheduling reasonably, so no technology mismatch flagged.

notes: Short conference-style paper with largely paraphrased/obfuscated prose; no quantitative results, statistics, sites, limitations or uncertainty reported. Q1 answered yes only because a working prototype and sensed data (Figures 4-5) are presented; the evidential content is minimal.
